A_target.statement: In the [[Definition:Untyped Lambda Calculus|$\lambda$-calculus]] with [[Definition:De Bruijn Index|de Bruijn indices]], [[Definition:Alpha Equivalence|$\alpha$-equivalent]] terms are syntactically identical, and substitution requires no renaming.

B_source.statement: In the [[Definition:Untyped Lambda Calculus|$\lambda$-calculus]] with named variables, [[Definition:Alpha Equivalence|$\alpha$-equivalence]] and [[Definition:Capture-Avoiding Substitution|capture-avoiding substitution]] are defined by explicit renaming of [[Definition:Bound Variable|bound variables]].

substitutions.a bound variable name: the number of binders between the variable and its own binder
substitutions.capture-avoiding renaming: index shifting when a term moves under a binder

derived.substitution defined with renaming: substitution defined with shifting, requiring no fresh-name generation
derived.reasoning up to alpha-equivalence: reasoning about concrete syntax trees, since the quotient is already taken

object_map.reformulation: Encode binding by position rather than by name, so that alpha-equivalence becomes literal equality.

validity_conditions: The translation is a bijection between alpha-equivalence classes of named terms and indexed terms, so nothing is lost and the quotient is built into the representation.
Reduction and typing rules transfer with renaming replaced by shifting, and the correspondence commutes with reduction.
The trade is legibility for mechanizability: indexed terms are far harder to read, and off-by-one shifting errors replace the capture errors that were eliminated.
proof_plan:
Replace each occurrence of a [[Definition:Bound Variable|bound variable]] by the number of binders crossed between it and its binder.
For example, $\lambda x. \lambda y. x$ becomes $\lambda. \lambda. 1$.
Define the shift $\map {\uparrow^d_c} t$, adding $d$ to every index $\ge c$ in $t$, to adjust indices when a term passes under a binder.

Restate substitution:
:$\paren {\lambda. t} \sqbrk {j := s} = \lambda. \paren {t \sqbrk {j + 1 := \map {\uparrow^1_0} s} }$
using shifting in place of capture-avoiding renaming.

By [[Principle of Structural Induction|induction]] on terms, the translation is a [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]] from [[Definition:Alpha Equivalence|$\alpha$-equivalence classes]] of named terms to indexed terms, and it commutes with [[Definition:Beta Reduction|$\beta$-reduction]].
{{qed}}
